For most small businesses, I'd recommend **Dropbox Sign, Zoho Sign or DocuSign**\. The best choice depends on how many contracts you send, your budget and whether you need features beyond collecting signatures.

If I were choosing for a small Australian business, here's how I'd compare them.

## Quick comparison

| Software | Best suited to | My verdict |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Dropbox Sign | Everyday contracts | Best simple option |
| Zoho Sign | Budget-conscious businesses | Best value |
| DocuSign | Professional agreements | Most established |
| PandaDoc | Quotes and proposals | Best document features |
| Annature | Australian businesses | Best local alternative |


## What I'd look for before buying

For a small business, I'd prioritise\:

1. **Unlimited or sufficient signing requests** – avoid getting caught by monthly document limits.
2. **Reusable templates** – save time on frequently used contracts.
3. **Automatic reminders** – chase unsigned documents automatically.
4. **Audit trails** – retain evidence of who signed and when.
5. **Easy customer experience** – customers should be able to sign on their phones without creating accounts.
6. **Australian compliance** – check whether the documents you need to sign can legally be signed electronically and whether any special signing requirements apply.

In Australia, electronic signatures are recognised for most Commonwealth legal processes under the Electronic Transactions Act 1999, subject to exceptions and other applicable requirements. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/legal-system/electronic-signatures-documents-and-transactions?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/legal-system/electronic-signatures-documents-and-transactions/electronic-signatures?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
